title: Toxoplasmosis in Dogs: New Study Links the Parasite to Eye Disease
seoTitle: Toxoplasmosis in Dogs: Eye Disease Study
description: Toxoplasmosis in dogs may cause uveitis, retinal detachment and blindness, a 2026 Hebrew University study of five dogs suggests. Signs, treatment and limits.

faq.a: Yes. Cats are the only animals in which the parasite completes its life cycle, but dogs and other warm-blooded animals can be infected, mainly through undercooked meat or food and water contaminated with cat feces. Most healthy adult dogs show no signs.

faq.q: Can toxoplasmosis make a dog blind?
faq.a: A 2026 study of five dogs in Israel suggests it can. Two dogs lost sight in one eye after retinal detachment, one went suddenly blind in both eyes and later recovered vision, and one blind eye had to be removed.

faq.q: How is toxoplasmosis in dogs' eyes treated?
faq.a: In the study, every dog received the antibiotic clindamycin by mouth plus anti-inflammatory eye drops chosen by a vet. All improved at first, but two relapsed, so follow-up checks matter.

faq.q: Are French Bulldogs at higher risk of toxoplasmosis?
faq.a: There is no evidence of that. None of the five dogs in the study was a French Bulldog. Dogs with a weakened immune system are at higher risk of severe disease, whatever their breed.

faq.q: What eye signs need a vet right away?
faq.a: Sudden vision loss is an emergency. A red, painful or cloudy eye also needs a prompt veterinary exam, especially in a dog on steroids or other immune-suppressing drugs.
